item.meaning: Ashoka's policy of ethical conduct, compassion, non-violence (Ahimsa), and mutual respect among religions.
Special senior officers appointed by Emperor Ashoka to teach and implement Dhamma policies across provinces.

item.definition: A vast political state comprising multiple kingdoms, diverse regions, and ethnic groups unified under an Emperor.

item.role_significance: Chief strategist who mentored Chandragupta Maurya and authored the 'Arthashastra', a comprehensive manual on statecraft and economic administration.
Mauryan Emperor who renounced armed military conquest ('Digvijaya') after the Kalinga War to promote ethical governance ('Dhammavijaya').

item.geographical_historical_significance: Capital of the Magadha, Mauryan, and Gupta Empires, located at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers as a water-fortress.

item.event_description: Founding of the Mauryan Empire by Chandragupta Maurya after defeating the Nanda dynasty.
The Kalinga War fought by Emperor Ashoka, leading to his adoption of Buddhism and non-violent Dhamma.

item.cause: Kalinga War slaughter (100,000 deaths and 150,000 deportations)
item.effect: Emperor Ashoka experienced deep remorse, converted to Buddhism, and abandoned armed conquest in favor of Dhamma.

item.significance: Ashoka's shift from military conquest by force (Digvijaya) to conquest by morality and righteousness (Dhamma Vijaya).
